prompt: We need to ___ a decision by Friday.
explanation: Both “make” and “take” exist, but “make a decision” is by far the default in all varieties of English. “Take a decision” is mainly British and more formal. French “prendre” pulls you towards “take”.

prompt: If we don't cut the scope, there's no way we'll ___ the deadline.
answers: meet
make
hit
explanation: You meet / make / hit a deadline. You miss it when you fail. “Respect a deadline” is a French calque.

trap.explanation: English meets (or hits) deadlines. “Respecter une échéance” doesn't translate word for word.

prompt: It is too early to ___ any firm conclusions from such a small sample.
explanation: Conclusions are DRAWN (you pull them out of the evidence). “Reach a conclusion” is also natural. “Take a conclusion” doesn't exist.

prompt: Experts say deepfakes ___ a serious threat to democratic debate.
explanation: Threats, risks, challenges and questions are POSED. It's formal/journalistic. In conversation you'd more often say “are a serious threat”.

prompt: ___ in mind that the exam covers the whole semester, not just the last chapters.
answers: bear
keep
explanation: “Bear in mind” / “keep in mind” = remember and take into account. “Bear” is slightly more formal.

prompt: The board was ___ disappointed with the quarterly results.
explanation: Adverb + adjective pairs are fixed: bitterly disappointed, deeply concerned, highly unlikely, strongly opposed, heavily criticised. “Very” works everywhere, but these pairs are what make writing sound native.

prompt: The flight was delayed because of ___ rain.
explanation: Rain, traffic, smoking and drinking are “heavy”. Wind, coffee and accents are “strong”. French “forte pluie” suggests “strong”.

trap.explanation: Rain is heavy, not strong (strong wind, heavy rain).
trap.frenchHint: Il y avait une forte pluie.

prompt: The model doesn't take ___ account seasonal variations in demand.
answers: into
explanation: Take something INTO account (into = movement inside the calculation). French “tenir compte de” often produces “take in account”.

trap.wrong: We must take in account the costs.
trap.correct: We must take the costs into account.
trap.frenchHint: Nous devons tenir compte des coûts.

prompt: After three hours of discussion, the team finally ___ a consensus.
explanation: You REACH a consensus / an agreement / a compromise / a verdict (the image of arriving at a destination).

prompt: Most people who ___ fraud online are never caught.
explanation: You commit crimes, fraud, errors (formal), suicide. French “faire une fraude” doesn't transfer.

prompt: Sleep deprivation has a measurable ___ on memory consolidation.
explanation: Usually: AFFECT is the verb (it affects memory), EFFECT is the noun (an effect on memory). A: action; E: end result.
compare: Sleep has an effect on memory.
(rare) to effect change = to bring about change

prompt: Buying a used laptop turned out to be the most ___ option.
explanation: ECONOMICAL = cheap to run / not wasteful. ECONOMIC = related to the economy (economic growth). FINANCIAL = money matters in general. FISCAL = government taxes and spending.

prompt: From his silence, I ___ that he disagreed.
explanation: The speaker IMPLIES (puts the meaning in). The listener INFERS (takes the meaning out).

prompt: The ___ interruptions from notifications made it impossible to focus.
explanation: CONTINUAL = repeated again and again, with breaks (often annoying). CONTINUOUS = without any break (a continuous line, continuous integration).

prompt: The treaty was signed at a ___ summit in Paris.
explanation: HISTORIC = important, remembered in history. HISTORICAL = related to the past or to history as a subject (historical records, a historical novel).

instruction: Which sentence means “Currently, I'm working on the backend”?
options: Actually, I'm working on the backend.
At the moment, I'm working on the backend.
Eventually, I'm working on the backend.
explanation: “Actually” = en fait (correction or surprise). “Actuellement” = currently / at the moment. “Eventually” = finalement.

trap.wrong: Actually, I work at a startup. (meaning: currently)
trap.correct: Currently, I work at a startup.
trap.frenchHint: Actuellement, je travaille dans une startup.

prompt: We could ___ add a dark mode later, if users ask for it.
explanation: “Eventually” means “in the end, after a long time”. French “éventuellement” = possibly / if necessary.

trap.wrong: We could eventually add a dark mode, if needed.
trap.correct: We could possibly add a dark mode, if needed.
trap.frenchHint: On pourrait éventuellement ajouter un mode sombre.

instruction: Click the part that contains an error (or “No error”).
explanation: “Assist” = help. “Assister à” = attend (no preposition).

instruction: Your friend cries at every film. She is very…
explanation: SENSITIVE = sensible (émotif, réactif). SENSIBLE = raisonnable, sensé.

prompt: The audit gave us a comprehensive overview of our security risks.
explanation: COMPREHENSIVE = complet, exhaustif. “Compréhensif” = understanding. “Compréhensible” = comprehensible / understandable.

prompt: Nous avons réalisé ce projet en six semaines.
answers: We carried out this project in six weeks.
We completed this project in six weeks.
We completed the project in six weeks.
We carried out the project in six weeks.
We did this project in six weeks.
We built this project in six weeks.
We delivered this project in six weeks.
model: We completed this project in six weeks.
explanation: “Realise” means “se rendre compte”. To “réaliser” a project: complete, carry out, build, deliver. On a CV: “Built…”, “Delivered…”.

trap.wrong: We realised this project in six weeks.
trap.correct: We completed this project in six weeks.
trap.explanation: “Realise” = se rendre compte. A project is completed / carried out / delivered.
trap.frenchHint: Nous avons réalisé ce projet en six semaines.

prompt: J'ai un contrôle de maths demain.
answers: I have a maths test tomorrow.
I've got a maths test tomorrow.
I have a math test tomorrow.
I have a maths exam tomorrow.
I've got a maths exam tomorrow.
model: I've got a maths test tomorrow.
explanation: “Control” means power / regulation (quality control, control over). An exam at school is a test, exam or quiz.

instruction: Complete with raise or rise, in the correct form.
prompt: Energy prices have ___ sharply since the beginning of the year.
answers: risen
explanation: RISE is intransitive (prices rise, rose, have risen). RAISE takes an object (they raised prices, raised a question).

prompt: The ___ of least privilege says each process should only get the permissions it needs.
answers: principle
explanation: PRINCIPLE = a rule or belief. PRINCIPAL = main (adjective), or the head of a school.

prompt: Her design skills ___ his technical background perfectly.
answers: complement
explanation: COMPLEMENT = complete / go well with (it completes). COMPLIMENT = praise.

prompt: She gave me some good advices about the interview.
answers: She gave me some good advice about the interview.
She gave me some good pieces of advice about the interview.
She gave me a good piece of advice about the interview.
model: She gave me some good advice about the interview.
explanation: “Advice” is uncountable. To count it: a piece of advice, two tips.
